sources.entry: NitroShare - Transferring files from one device to another

summary.one_liner: NitroShare is a cross-platform desktop application for transferring files and directories between devices on the same local network, with automatic device discovery.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes NitroShare as a network file transfer app for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It automatically discovers devices on the local network and lets users transfer individual files or entire directories between them. Transfers can optionally be encrypted with TLS, and the app exposes a local HTTP API. The README says the project is free and open-source and points to the NitroShare website for downloads and the GitHub wiki for build instructions and protocol descriptions. The README does not describe the internal workings of the app beyond these points.
use_cases: Transfer files between computers on the same network
Send entire folders to another device without cloud upload
Share files between Windows, macOS, and Linux machines
Automate local transfers via the HTTP API
Encrypt file transfers on a local network
how_to_run: Download the application from the NitroShare website (link not included in the README text)
For building from source, see the instructions on the GitHub wiki
notable: Automatic discovery of devices on the local network
Transfers entire directories, not just single files
caveats: Development has been on hold for several years; the README says there are no current plans to continue the C++ codebase
Development is resuming in a separate project, nitroshare/nitroshare2, and a new desktop client is promised only after that codebase is stable
Build instructions and protocol details are on the GitHub wiki rather than in the README
